literal: Even if they do painful things like killing, upon remembering one good deed done by them, [the pain] will disappear.
translation: Even if someone does you harm as painful as murder, all that suffering will vanish the moment you remember a single good deed they did for you in the past.
modern: கொலை செய்வதைப் போன்ற துன்பங்களை ஒருவர் நமக்குச் செய்தாலும், அவர் முன்பு செய்த ஒரு நன்மையை நினைத்துப் பார்த்தால் அந்தத் துன்பங்கள் மறைந்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme power of gratitude in overcoming resentment. The poet uses a powerful comparison: even if someone inflicts a harm so severe that it feels like being killed ('koṉṟu aṉṉa iṉṉā'), we should not harbor hatred. Instead, by actively remembering ('uḷḷa') even a single good deed ('oṉṟu naṉṟu') that person did for us in the past, the pain and anger caused by their massive harm will completely vanish ('keṭum'). This teaches us that gratitude has the strength to dissolve even the deepest grievances.
